# Terraform plan on PR, apply on merge to main (dev environment).
name: terraform

on:
  pull_request:
    paths: ['infra/**']
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths: ['infra/**']

permissions:
  contents: read
  id-token: write
  pull-requests: write

jobs:
  plan:
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        env: [dev, staging, prod]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: infra/environments/${{ matrix.env }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: hashicorp/setup-terraform@v3
        with: { terraform_version: '1.9.8' }
      - uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v4
        with:
          role-to-assume: arn:aws:iam::${{ vars.AWS_ACCOUNT_ID }}:role/gha-tf-plan
          aws-region: ${{ vars.AWS_REGION }}
      - run: terraform fmt -check -recursive ../..
      - run: terraform init -backend-config="key=envs/${{ matrix.env }}/terraform.tfstate"
      - run: terraform validate
      - run: terraform plan -no-color -out=tfplan
      - name: Post plan to PR
        uses: actions/github-script@v7
        with:
          script: |
            const { stdout } = await exec.getExecOutput('terraform', ['show', '-no-color', 'tfplan'], { cwd: 'infra/environments/${{ matrix.env }}' });
            const body = `### tf plan — ${{ matrix.env }}\n\n<details><summary>plan</summary>\n\n\`\`\`hcl\n${stdout.slice(0, 60000)}\n\`\`\`\n</details>`;
            github.rest.issues.createComment({ issue_number: context.issue.number, owner: context.repo.owner, repo: context.repo.repo, body });

  apply-dev:
    if: github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: dev-infra
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: infra/environments/dev
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: hashicorp/setup-terraform@v3
        with: { terraform_version: '1.9.8' }
      - uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v4
        with:
          role-to-assume: arn:aws:iam::${{ vars.AWS_ACCOUNT_ID }}:role/gha-tf-apply
          aws-region: ${{ vars.AWS_REGION }}
      - run: terraform init -backend-config="key=envs/dev/terraform.tfstate"
      - run: terraform apply -auto-approve

# Python (FastAPI / Flask / Django) CI template.
# Copy to .github/workflows/ci.yml. Adjust paths, secret names, deploy targets.
name: ci

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    tags: ['v*']

permissions:
  contents: read
  id-token: write
  packages: write
  pull-requests: write

concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

env:
  PYTHON_VERSION: '3.12'

jobs:
  lint:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: ${{ env.PYTHON_VERSION }}
          cache: pip
      - run: pip install uv
      - run: uv sync --frozen
      - run: uv run ruff check .
      - run: uv run ruff format --check .

  typecheck:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: ${{ env.PYTHON_VERSION }}
          cache: pip
      - run: pip install uv && uv sync --frozen
      - run: uv run mypy src tests

  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    services:
      postgres:
        image: pgvector/pgvector:pg16
        env:
          POSTGRES_USER: test
          POSTGRES_PASSWORD: test
          POSTGRES_DB: test
        ports: ['5432:5432']
        options: >-
          --health-cmd "pg_isready -U test"
          --health-interval 5s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 10
      redis:
        image: redis:7-alpine
        ports: ['6379:6379']
    env:
      DATABASE_URL: postgresql+asyncpg://test:test@localhost:5432/test
      REDIS_URL: redis://localhost:6379/0
      JWT_SECRET: ci-test-secret
      ENV: test
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: ${{ env.PYTHON_VERSION }}
          cache: pip
      - run: pip install uv && uv sync --frozen
      - run: uv run alembic upgrade head
      - run: uv run pytest --cov=src --cov-report=xml --cov-fail-under=80
      - uses: codecov/codecov-action@v4
        if: always()
        with:
          files: coverage.xml
          fail_ci_if_error: false

  build:
    needs: [lint, typecheck, test]
    if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      image: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.tags }}
      digest: ${{ steps.push.outputs.digest }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3
      - uses: docker/login-action@v3
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      - id: meta
        uses: docker/metadata-action@v5
        with:
          images: ghcr.io/${{ github.repository }}/api
          tags: |
            type=sha,prefix=sha-
            type=semver,pattern={{version}}
            type=raw,value=latest,enable=${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' }}
      - id: push
        uses: docker/build-push-action@v6
        with:
          context: ./apps/api
          push: true
          tags: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.tags }}
          labels: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.labels }}
          cache-from: type=gha
          cache-to: type=gha,mode=max
          provenance: true
          sbom: true

  scan:
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: aquasecurity/trivy-action@0.24.0
        with:
          image-ref: ${{ needs.build.outputs.image }}
          severity: 'CRITICAL,HIGH'
          exit-code: '1'
          ignore-unfixed: true

# Deploy to AWS ECS via OIDC. Trigger: push to main (dev) and tag v* (prod).
name: deploy

on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: [ci]
    types: [completed]
    branches: [main]
  push:
    tags: ['v*']

permissions:
  id-token: write
  contents: read

jobs:
  deploy-dev:
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_run' && github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: dev
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v4
        with:
          role-to-assume: arn:aws:iam::${{ vars.AWS_ACCOUNT_ID }}:role/gha-deploy-dev
          aws-region: ${{ vars.AWS_REGION }}
      - name: Update ECS service
        run: |
          aws ecs update-service \
            --cluster ${{ vars.ECS_CLUSTER_DEV }} \
            --service ${{ vars.ECS_SERVICE }} \
            --force-new-deployment \
            --query 'service.serviceArn' --output text
      - name: Wait for stable
        run: |
          aws ecs wait services-stable \
            --cluster ${{ vars.ECS_CLUSTER_DEV }} \
            --services ${{ vars.ECS_SERVICE }}

  deploy-prod:
    if: startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment:
      name: prod
      url: ${{ vars.PROD_URL }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v4
        with:
          role-to-assume: arn:aws:iam::${{ vars.AWS_ACCOUNT_ID_PROD }}:role/gha-deploy-prod
          aws-region: ${{ vars.AWS_REGION }}
      - name: Update ECS service
        run: |
          aws ecs update-service \
            --cluster ${{ vars.ECS_CLUSTER_PROD }} \
            --service ${{ vars.ECS_SERVICE }} \
            --force-new-deployment
      - name: Wait for stable
        run: |
          aws ecs wait services-stable \
            --cluster ${{ vars.ECS_CLUSTER_PROD }} \
            --services ${{ vars.ECS_SERVICE }}

# Go (Gin / Echo / chi) CI template.
name: ci

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    tags: ['v*']

permissions:
  contents: read
  id-token: write
  packages: write

concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

env:
  GO_VERSION: '1.23'

jobs:
  lint:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-go@v5
        with:
          go-version: ${{ env.GO_VERSION }}
          cache: true
      - uses: golangci/golangci-lint-action@v6
        with: { version: v1.61 }

  vet:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-go@v5
        with:
          go-version: ${{ env.GO_VERSION }}
          cache: true
      - run: go vet ./...
      - run: go install honnef.co/go/tools/cmd/staticcheck@latest
      - run: staticcheck ./...

  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    services:
      postgres:
        image: pgvector/pgvector:pg16
        env:
          POSTGRES_USER: test
          POSTGRES_PASSWORD: test
          POSTGRES_DB: test
        ports: ['5432:5432']
        options: >-
          --health-cmd "pg_isready -U test"
          --health-interval 5s
          --health-retries 10
    env:
      DATABASE_URL: postgres://test:test@localhost:5432/test?sslmode=disable
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-go@v5
        with:
          go-version: ${{ env.GO_VERSION }}
          cache: true
      - run: go test -race -coverprofile=coverage.out -covermode=atomic ./...
      - run: |
          go tool cover -func=coverage.out | awk '/^total:/ {gsub("%","",$3); if ($3+0 < 80) {print "coverage " $3 "% < 80"; exit 1}}'

  build:
    needs: [lint, vet, test]
    if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      image: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.tags }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3
      - uses: docker/login-action@v3
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      - id: meta
        uses: docker/metadata-action@v5
        with:
          images: ghcr.io/${{ github.repository }}/api
          tags: |
            type=sha,prefix=sha-
            type=semver,pattern={{version}}
            type=raw,value=latest,enable=${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' }}
      - uses: docker/build-push-action@v6
        with:
          context: ./apps/api
          push: true
          tags: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.tags }}
          labels: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.labels }}
          cache-from: type=gha
          cache-to: type=gha,mode=max
          provenance: true
          sbom: true

  scan:
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: aquasecurity/trivy-action@0.24.0
        with:
          image-ref: ${{ needs.build.outputs.image }}
          severity: 'CRITICAL,HIGH'
          exit-code: '1'
          ignore-unfixed: true

# Node (Next.js / NestJS / Express / Hono) CI template.
name: ci

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    tags: ['v*']

permissions:
  contents: read
  id-token: write
  packages: write

concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

env:
  NODE_VERSION: '20'

jobs:

          cache: pnpm
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      - run: pnpm lint
      - run: pnpm format --check

  typecheck:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
        with: { version: 9 }
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: ${{ env.NODE_VERSION }}
          cache: pnpm
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      - run: pnpm typecheck

  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    services:
      postgres:
        image: pgvector/pgvector:pg16
        env:
          POSTGRES_USER: test
          POSTGRES_PASSWORD: test
          POSTGRES_DB: test
        ports: ['5432:5432']
        options: >-
          --health-cmd "pg_isready -U test"
          --health-interval 5s
          --health-retries 10
      redis:
        image: redis:7-alpine
        ports: ['6379:6379']
    env:
      DATABASE_URL: postgresql://test:test@localhost:5432/test
      REDIS_URL: redis://localhost:6379/0
      NODE_ENV: test
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
        with: { version: 9 }
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: ${{ env.NODE_VERSION }}
          cache: pnpm
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      - run: pnpm test -- --run --coverage
      - uses: codecov/codecov-action@v4
        if: always()
        with: { files: coverage/lcov.info }

  e2e:
    needs: [lint, typecheck, test]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
        with: { version: 9 }
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: ${{ env.NODE_VERSION }}
          cache: pnpm
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      - run: pnpm exec playwright install --with-deps
      - run: pnpm playwright test
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        if: failure()
        with:
          name: playwright-report
          path: playwright-report

  build:
    needs: [lint, typecheck, test]
    if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      image: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.tags }}
    steps:

        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      - id: meta
        uses: docker/metadata-action@v5
        with:
          images: ghcr.io/${{ github.repository }}/web
          tags: |
            type=sha,prefix=sha-
            type=semver,pattern={{version}}
            type=raw,value=latest,enable=${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' }}
      - uses: docker/build-push-action@v6

          context: ./apps/web
          push: true
          tags: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.tags }}
          labels: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.labels }}
          cache-from: type=gha
          cache-to: type=gha,mode=max
          provenance: true
          sbom: true

  scan:
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: aquasecurity/trivy-action@0.24.0

# Terraform module stubs

Copy-and-adapt modules. Each is a starting point — production deployments
should review variables, IAM, tagging, monitoring, and lifecycle.

## Modules

| Module                | Purpose                                          |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `network-aws/`        | VPC + public/private subnets + NAT (single or HA)|
| `ecs-service-aws/`    | Fargate service + task roles + CW logs + secrets |
| `rds-postgres-aws/`   | RDS Postgres + backups + Secrets Manager DSN     |

## Usage pattern

```hcl
module "network" {
  source = "../../../skill/assets/terraform-modules/network-aws"
  name   = "softco-${var.env}"
  cidr   = "10.10.0.0/16"
  ha_nat = var.env == "prod"
  tags   = local.tags
}

module "db" {
  source                 = "../../../skill/assets/terraform-modules/rds-postgres-aws"
  name                   = "softco-${var.env}"
  env                    = var.env
  multi_az               = var.env == "prod"
  subnet_ids             = module.network.private_subnet_ids
  vpc_security_group_ids = [module.network.db_sg_id]
  tags                   = local.tags
}

module "api" {
  source             = "../../../skill/assets/terraform-modules/ecs-service-aws"
  name               = "api-${var.env}"
  env                = var.env
  cluster_arn        = aws_ecs_cluster.this.arn
  container_image    = "${var.ecr_repo}:${var.image_tag}"
  subnet_ids         = module.network.private_subnet_ids
  security_group_ids = [module.network.app_sg_id]
  secret_arns        = { DATABASE_URL = module.db.connection_secret_arn }
  tags               = local.tags
}
```

## Notes

- These modules are AWS-only. GCP/Azure/DO equivalents follow the same shape
  — adapt or generate on demand.
- Run `tflint` + `tfsec` against the calling environment, not the modules in
  isolation.
- KMS, S3 backend, DynamoDB lock are environment-level, not module-level.
- Outputs are intentionally minimal — extend per project.

# Multi-stage Dockerfile for FastAPI services.
# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1.7

FROM python:3.12-slim AS builder
ENV PIP_NO_CACHE_DIR=1 \
    PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 \
    UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT=/opt/venv
WORKDIR /app
RUN apt-get update \
 && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends build-essential curl ca-certificates \
 && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir uv
COPY pyproject.toml uv.lock ./
RUN uv sync --frozen --no-dev
COPY src/ ./src/
COPY alembic.ini ./
COPY migrations/ ./migrations/

FROM python:3.12-slim AS runtime
ENV PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 \
    PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 \
    PATH="/opt/venv/bin:$PATH" \
    PORT=8000
WORKDIR /app
RUN apt-get update \
 && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends curl ca-certificates \
 && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* \
 && useradd -r -u 1001 -g root app
COPY --from=builder /opt/venv /opt/venv
COPY --from=builder /app /app
USER 1001
EXPOSE 8000
HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=5s --start-period=20s --retries=3 \
  CMD curl -fsS "http://127.0.0.1:${PORT}/health" || exit 1
CMD ["uvicorn", "src.main:app", "--host", "0.0.0.0", "--port", "8000", "--workers", "2"]

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# install.sh — install SoftCo skill to all supported agent paths
#
# Usage:
#   ./install.sh              # install to all agents (symlinks)
#   ./install.sh --agent NAME # install to one agent (claude|opencode|codex|gemini|openclaw)
#   ./install.sh --uninstall  # remove from all agents
#   ./install.sh --force      # overwrite existing installs
#   ./install.sh --copy       # copy files instead of symlinking

set -euo pipefail

err() { printf '\033[31m[install]\033[0m %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit 1; }
ok()  { printf '\033[32m[install]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
log() { printf '[install] %s\n' "$*"; }

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" &>/dev/null && pwd)"
SKILL="softco"
SKILL_SRC="$SCRIPT_DIR/skill"

UNINSTALL=0
FORCE=0
COPY=0
TARGET_AGENT=""

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --uninstall) UNINSTALL=1 ;;
    --force)     FORCE=1 ;;
    --copy)      COPY=1 ;;
    --agent)     TARGET_AGENT="${2:-}"; shift ;;
    -h|--help)   sed -n '2,7p' "$0"; exit 0 ;;
    *)           err "unknown flag: $1" ;;
  esac
  shift
done

[[ $UNINSTALL -eq 0 ]] && {
  [[ -d "$SKILL_SRC" ]]          || err "source dir missing: $SKILL_SRC"
  [[ -f "$SKILL_SRC/SKILL.md" ]] || err "SKILL.md missing at $SKILL_SRC/SKILL.md"
}

handle() {
  local name="$1" dest="$2"
  [[ -n "$TARGET_AGENT" && "$name" != "$TARGET_AGENT" ]] && return

  if [[ $UNINSTALL -eq 1 ]]; then
    if [[ -L "$dest" || -e "$dest" ]]; then
      rm -rf -- "$dest"
      ok "[$name] removed $dest"
    else
      log "[$name] nothing at $dest"
    fi
    return
  fi

  if [[ -L "$dest" && "$(readlink "$dest")" == "$SKILL_SRC" ]]; then
    ok "[$name] already installed → $dest"; return
  fi

  if [[ -L "$dest" || -e "$dest" ]]; then
    if [[ $FORCE -eq 1 ]]; then rm -rf -- "$dest"
    else log "[$name] exists (use --force to overwrite): $dest"; return
    fi
  fi

  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$dest")"
  if [[ $COPY -eq 1 ]]; then
    cp -r "$SKILL_SRC" "$dest"
    ok "[$name] copied: $dest"
  else
    ln -s "$SKILL_SRC" "$dest"
    ok "[$name] installed: $dest → $SKILL_SRC"
  fi
}

handle "claude"   "${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}/skills/$SKILL"
handle "opencode" "${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/opencode/skills/$SKILL"
handle "codex"    "$HOME/.agents/skills/$SKILL"
handle "gemini"   "$HOME/.gemini/antigravity/skills/$SKILL"
handle "openclaw" "$HOME/.openclaw/workspace/skills/$SKILL"

[[ $UNINSTALL -eq 0 ]] && log "restart your agent session to load the skill"

# Multi-stage Dockerfile for Go services. Distroless final, statically linked.
# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1.7

FROM golang:1.23-bookworm AS builder
WORKDIR /src
ENV CGO_ENABLED=0 GOOS=linux GOFLAGS="-trimpath"
COPY go.mod go.sum ./
RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/go/pkg/mod go mod download
COPY . .
RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/go/pkg/mod \
    --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.cache/go-build \
    go build -ldflags="-s -w -X main.version=${VERSION:-dev}" -o /out/api ./cmd/api

FROM gcr.io/distroless/static-debian12:nonroot
WORKDIR /
COPY --from=builder /out/api /api
EXPOSE 8000
USER nonroot:nonroot
ENTRYPOINT ["/api"]

# Release automation via Conventional Commits.
# release-please creates a PR that bumps version + writes CHANGELOG; merging
# that PR tags the release, which triggers deploy-prod.
name: release-please

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]

permissions:
  contents: write
  pull-requests: write

jobs:
  release:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: googleapis/release-please-action@v4
        with:
          release-type: simple
          package-name: ${{ github.event.repository.name }}

# SoftCo — Autonomous AI Coding Agent & Software Company Skill

[![GitHub stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/shihabshahrier/softco.svg)](https://github.com/shihabshahrier/softco/stargazers)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow.svg)](https://opensource.org/licenses/MIT)
[![Supported AI Agents](https://img.shields.io/badge/AI_Agents-Claude_Code_|_Cursor_|_Windsurf_|_Cline-blue.svg)](#agent-support)

Turn any AI coding agent (Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, Cline) into a complete, autonomous software company. The user describes their product or software idea; **SoftCo** handles the entire lifecycle: planning, system design, documentation, test-first coding, DevOps containerization, continuous integration, and automated deployment. The user only ever needs to configure the `.env` file.

## 🚀 What it is

An **Agent Skill** (supporting [Agent Skills](https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/claude-code/skills)) that transforms any supported large language model (LLM) agent or developer assistant into a fully-functional, autonomous software engineering firm. It simulates an entire development team: Product Manager, Software Architect, Senior Engineer, DevOps Engineer, QA Engineer, Security Expert, and Technical Writer. 

The agent operates under a highly-disciplined, professional software development lifecycle (SDLC) phase order:

```
Phase 0 → Phase 1 → Phase 2 → Phase 3 → Phase 4 → Phase 5 → Phase 6
Discovery  Design    Docs      Code      Test      Infra     Deploy
```

Documentation and tests come before code. Test coverage of ≥ 80% is strictly enforced. Secrets are never committed to git. Every project ships with a standardized `AGENT.md` contract file that lets a fresh agent session continue the work seamlessly without questions.

## 🚫 Prohibited Actions & Strict Guardrails

SoftCo strictly adheres to enterprise-grade engineering principles and **never**:
* Hardcodes API keys, secrets, or passwords (always uses Secrets Manager or `.env.example`).
* Runs unoptimized or dangerous database queries (e.g., `SELECT *` in production schemas).
* Skips the documentation first phase (SDLC rigor is always enforced).
* Merges to the `main` branch without passing linting, formatting, and test suites.
* Implements authentication from scratch when proven libraries exist (Clerk, NextAuth, Supabase).
* Deploys services without active health check and readiness probe endpoints.
* Generates `.env` files with plaintext production credentials.
* Allows un-typed or dangerous types (like `any` in TypeScript) in production code.

## Threat model checklist (every project)

Run this in Phase 1 and update each major change:

1. **Data classes**: public / internal / confidential / restricted. Where does
   each live? Encrypted at rest? In transit?
2. **Trust boundaries**: end-user, third-party API, internal services, admin.
3. **Entry points**: every public endpoint, webhook, file upload, queue,
   third-party callback.
4. **Identities**: human users, service accounts, agents (LLM tools).
5. **High-impact assets**: PII, payment, credentials, signing keys.
6. **Attack surface deltas**: what's new this release?

Output `docs/THREAT_MODEL.md` with a STRIDE table per entry point.

## OWASP Top 10 (2021) — defaults that block each

| Threat                          | Default control                                          |
| ------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| A01 Broken Access Control       | Server-side authz on every endpoint; tenant scoping; tests |
| A02 Cryptographic Failures      | TLS 1.2+ only; argon2id; KMS for keys                    |
| A03 Injection                   | Parameterised queries; Zod/Pydantic at boundary; escape outputs |
| A04 Insecure Design             | Threat model; ADRs; least privilege                      |
| A05 Security Misconfig          | Helmet/CSP; default-deny CORS; no debug in prod          |
| A06 Vulnerable Components       | Dependabot; weekly audit; image scan                     |
| A07 Auth Failures               | MFA; rate-limit; short JWT; refresh rotation; lockout    |
| A08 Software & Data Integrity   | Signed commits; SLSA-style provenance; pinned deps       |
| A09 Logging & Monitoring        | Structured logs; SIEM; alerting on auth anomalies        |
| A10 SSRF                        | Egress allowlist; metadata endpoint block; URL validation|

## Secrets management

Rules:
- **Never** commit secrets. Period.
- `.env` always gitignored. `.env.example` committed.
- Production secrets in cloud secrets manager (AWS SM / GCP SM / Azure KV /
  Vault).
- Rotate every 90 days; rotation hooks in Terraform where supported.
- Inject at runtime (ECS task secret refs, K8s External Secrets) — never bake
  into image.
- Logging filters strip known secret patterns.

Detection:
- `gitleaks` pre-commit hook
- `trufflehog` in CI
- GitHub secret scanning enabled + push protection

If a secret leaks: rotate immediately → invalidate exposed copies → audit
access logs → post-mortem in `docs/incidents/`.

---

## Authentication

### Defaults

- Library, not roll-your-own: Clerk / NextAuth / Supabase Auth / Auth0 /
  Cognito.
- If a library cannot be used:
  - Password hashing: argon2id (params: `t=2, m=64MiB, p=1` minimum)
  - JWT: HS256 with rotating key or RS256 with KMS; `exp` ≤ 1 hour
  - Refresh tokens: opaque, stored hashed, single-use rotation, family
    tracking for replay detection
  - Account lockout / progressive delay after N failed attempts
  - MFA via TOTP (RFC 6238) or WebAuthn

### JWT minimum claims

```json
{
  "iss": "softco-api",
  "sub": "<user-id>",
  "aud": "softco-web",
  "iat": 1715200000,
  "exp": 1715203600,
  "jti": "<unique-id>",
  "tenant_id": "<uuid>"
}
```

Validate every claim server-side, including `iss` and `aud`.

### Sessions vs JWT

- Web app + same-origin API → consider HttpOnly Secure SameSite=Strict
  session cookies + server-side store (Redis). Simpler revocation.
- Mobile / multi-client / cross-origin → JWT + short-lived access + rotating
  refresh.

## Authorization

Always enforced on the **server**. Client-side checks are UX only.

Patterns:
- **RBAC**: roles assigned to users; permissions assigned to roles
- **ABAC**: attribute-based for fine-grained ("owner can edit, viewer can
  read")
- **Tenant scoping**: every query includes `tenant_id`; enforce via RLS or
  middleware

Implementation rule: **deny by default**. Endpoint without explicit policy
returns 403.

```python
# api/deps.py
async def require_permission(perm: str):
    async def _dep(user: User = Depends(current_user)) -> User:
        if perm not in user.permissions:
            raise Forbidden(f"missing permission: {perm}")
        return user
    return _dep

# usage
@router.post("/projects/{id}/archive", dependencies=[Depends(require_permission("project:archive"))])
async def archive(...): ...
```

## Input validation

- Parse at boundary (Pydantic, Zod, struct + validator). Internal code trusts
  parsed types.
- Length caps on every string. Size caps on every payload.
- Allowlist over blocklist (file types, URL schemes, redirect targets).
- IDs in path/query validated as expected format before any DB lookup.

```python
class CreatePost(BaseModel):
    title: Annotated[str, StringConstraints(min_length=1, max_length=200)]
    body: Annotated[str, StringConstraints(min_length=1, max_length=10_000)]
    tags: Annotated[list[str], Field(max_length=10)]
```

---

## SQL injection

- Always parameterise. Never string-format SQL.
- ORM queries by default; raw SQL only with `:bind` params.
- Reject identifier interpolation from user input (table / column names).

```python
# good
await session.execute(text("SELECT id FROM users WHERE email = :e"), {"e": email})
# bad — never
session.execute(f"SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = '{email}'")
```

---

## XSS

- Never `innerHTML` / `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` with user input
- Use framework-default escaping (React auto-escapes)
- For markdown / rich text: render via library (`marked` + `DOMPurify`,
  `markdown-it` + sanitiser); allowlist tags + attrs
- CSP header that blocks inline scripts (or uses nonce-based inline)

```
Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'nonce-{n}';
  style-src 'self' 'nonce-{n}'; img-src 'self' data: https:; connect-src 'self' https://api.example.com;
  frame-ancestors 'none'; base-uri 'self'; object-src 'none'
```

---

## CSRF

- API uses Bearer JWT → CSRF immune (no cookie auth)
- API uses cookie → require `SameSite=Strict` and CSRF token on state-changing
  requests
- Webhook endpoints verify signature, not session

---

## Rate limiting

Every public endpoint. Layered:

- L7 edge: CloudFront / Cloud Armor / Nginx
- App: per-user + per-IP token bucket via Redis

```python
from fastapi import Depends
from slowapi import Limiter
from slowapi.util import get_remote_address

limiter = Limiter(key_func=get_remote_address)
# app.state.limiter = limiter; add SlowAPIMiddleware

@router.post("/auth/login")
@limiter.limit("5/minute")
async def login(...): ...
```

Stricter limits on `/auth/*` and `/password-reset`.

## CORS

Production: explicit allowlist of known origins. Never `*` with credentials.

```python
app.add_middleware(
    CORSMiddleware,
    allow_origins=["https://app.example.com"],
    allow_credentials=True,
    allow_methods=["GET", "POST", "PUT", "PATCH", "DELETE"],
    allow_headers=["Authorization", "Content-Type", "Idempotency-Key"],
    max_age=600,
)
```

## Security headers (set on every response)

| Header                              | Value                                  |
| ----------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| `Strict-Transport-Security`         | `max-age=63072000; includeSubDomains; preload` |
| `X-Content-Type-Options`            | `nosniff`                              |
| `X-Frame-Options`                   | `DENY`                                 |
| `Referrer-Policy`                   | `strict-origin-when-cross-origin`      |
| `Permissions-Policy`                | `camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=()` (tune per app) |
| `Content-Security-Policy`           | see above                              |
| `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy`        | `same-origin`                          |
| `Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy`      | `same-origin`                          |

---

## File uploads

- Allowlist MIME + extension; verify magic bytes
- Cap size at the proxy + app level
- Scan with ClamAV / cloud AV before exposing
- Store in S3 / GCS with random keys; never the original filename
- Serve via signed URLs with short TTL
- Never serve uploads from the app origin without `Content-Disposition:
  attachment` + sandboxed subdomain

---

## SSRF defence

When fetching URLs supplied by users (webhooks, image proxy, OG preview):

- Allowlist schemes (`http`, `https` only)
- Resolve DNS, reject private CIDRs (`10/8`, `172.16/12`, `192.168/16`,
  `169.254.169.254`, `127/8`)
- Bind outbound to a non-default egress with metadata blocked
- Timeout + size cap on the response

---

## Supply chain

- Pin all dependencies (lockfile committed)
- Verify integrity (npm `--frozen-lockfile`, `uv sync --frozen`)
- Signed container images (cosign) where infra supports it
- SBOM generated in CI (`docker build --sbom=true`)
- Renovate / Dependabot weekly
- Trivy image scan blocks on HIGH+

---

## Logging — what NOT to log

Never log:
- Passwords, tokens, keys
- Full credit card / bank account
- Session cookies
- Authorization headers
- LLM-generated user PII without redaction

Log:
- User ID (opaque), request ID, route, method, status, duration
- Auth events: login success/fail, MFA, password reset
- Authz failures with reason

---

## AI-specific risks

- **Prompt injection**: input filtering + system prompt design + output
  validation. Never give an injectable LLM admin-level tools.
- **Data exfiltration via tool**: tools that fetch URLs / make API calls must
  allowlist destinations and redact secrets.
- **Model output trust**: never `exec` / `eval` LLM output. Never use it as
  SQL / shell / file paths without schema validation.
- **PII leak**: redact before sending to third-party models if data residency
  matters.
- **Token cost DOS**: per-user rate limit + budget cap.

---

## Incident response

When an issue is reported / detected:

1. Triage severity (data loss / outage / leak / minor)
2. Contain — rotate creds, disable feature, scale down attacker
3. Eradicate — patch, redeploy
4. Recover — restore, monitor
5. Post-mortem in `docs/incidents/YYYYMMDD-<slug>.md`:
   - Timeline
   - Root cause
   - Impact
   - Detection delay
   - Action items with owners + dates
6. Track action items to completion

---

## Compliance quick-map

| Regime  | Key controls                                                  |
| ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| GDPR    | Lawful basis; DPA; data export + erase; breach notification 72h |
| HIPAA   | BAA with vendors; encryption at rest + transit; audit logs    |
| SOC2    | Access reviews; change mgmt; monitoring; vendor mgmt          |
| PCI-DSS | Tokenise card data; segment cardholder env; logging; quarterly scans |

Confirm scope with user before claiming compliance. Most projects need
**GDPR-ready posture** even if not formally certified.

---

## Never do

- Roll your own crypto
- Disable TLS verification in any prod code
- `eval` / `exec` of any user-derived string
- Wide-open S3 / GCS buckets
- IAM `*` in prod
- Skipping the rate-limiter on auth endpoints
- Logging PII without redaction
- Trusting client-supplied user ID / role / tenant ID

## Standard pipeline

```
trigger:
  pull_request → main
  push         → main
  tag          → v*.*.*

jobs:
  lint
  type-check
  test (unit + integration)
  build (docker image)
  scan (trivy)
  push (registry)
  deploy-dev   (on push to main)
  e2e          (against dev URL)
  deploy-prod  (on tag, with approval)
```

All jobs run on `pull_request` except `push`, `deploy-*`, `e2e`.

---

## Reusable workflow — full template

```yaml
# .github/workflows/ci.yml
name: ci

on:
  pull_request:
  push: { branches: [main], tags: ['v*'] }

permissions:
  contents: read
  id-token: write       # OIDC for cloud auth
  packages: write       # GHCR push
  pull-requests: write  # PR comments

concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

jobs:
  lint:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with: { python-version: '3.12', cache: 'pip' }
      - run: pip install uv && uv sync --frozen
      - run: uv run ruff check .
      - run: uv run ruff format --check .

  typecheck:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with: { python-version: '3.12', cache: 'pip' }
      - run: pip install uv && uv sync --frozen
      - run: uv run mypy src tests

  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    services:
      postgres:
        image: pgvector/pgvector:pg16
        env:
          POSTGRES_USER: test
          POSTGRES_PASSWORD: test
          POSTGRES_DB: test
        ports: ['5432:5432']
        options: >-
          --health-cmd "pg_isready -U test"
          --health-interval 5s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 10
      redis:
        image: redis:7-alpine
        ports: ['6379:6379']
    env:
      DATABASE_URL: postgresql+asyncpg://test:test@localhost:5432/test
      REDIS_URL: redis://localhost:6379/0
      JWT_SECRET: ci-test-secret-do-not-use-in-prod
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with: { python-version: '3.12', cache: 'pip' }
      - run: pip install uv && uv sync --frozen
      - run: uv run alembic upgrade head
      - run: uv run pytest --cov=src --cov-report=xml --cov-fail-under=80
      - uses: codecov/codecov-action@v4
        with: { files: coverage.xml, fail_ci_if_error: true }

  build:
    needs: [lint, typecheck, test]
    if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs: { image: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.tags }} }
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3
      - uses: docker/login-action@v3
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      - id: meta
        uses: docker/metadata-action@v5
        with:
          images: ghcr.io/${{ github.repository }}/api
          tags: |
            type=sha,prefix=sha-
            type=semver,pattern={{version}}
            type=raw,value=latest,enable=${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' }}
      - uses: docker/build-push-action@v6
        with:
          context: ./apps/api
          push: true
          tags: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.tags }}
          labels: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.labels }}
          cache-from: type=gha
          cache-to: type=gha,mode=max
          provenance: true
          sbom: true

  scan:
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: aquasecurity/trivy-action@0.24.0
        with:
          image-ref: ${{ needs.build.outputs.image }}
          severity: 'CRITICAL,HIGH'
          exit-code: '1'
          ignore-unfixed: true

  deploy-dev:
    needs: [build, scan]
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: dev
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v4
        with:
          role-to-assume: arn:aws:iam::${{ vars.AWS_ACCOUNT_ID }}:role/gha-deploy-dev
          aws-region: us-east-1
      - run: |
          aws ecs update-service --cluster softco-dev --service api \
            --force-new-deployment --query 'service.serviceArn' --output text

  e2e:
    needs: deploy-dev
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with: { node-version: '20', cache: 'pnpm' }
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      - run: pnpm playwright install --with-deps
      - run: pnpm playwright test
        env: { BASE_URL: https://dev.example.com }
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        if: failure()
        with: { name: playwright-report, path: playwright-report }

  deploy-prod:
    needs: [build, scan]
    if: startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment:
      name: prod
      url: https://example.com
    steps:
      - uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v4
        with:
          role-to-assume: arn:aws:iam::${{ vars.AWS_ACCOUNT_ID_PROD }}:role/gha-deploy-prod
          aws-region: us-east-1
      - run: |
          aws ecs update-service --cluster softco-prod --service api \
            --force-new-deployment
```

`environment: prod` triggers GitHub approval gate (configured per env in
repo Settings → Environments).

## Cloud auth — OIDC, never long-lived keys

### AWS

Create role + trust policy in Terraform:

```hcl
data "aws_iam_openid_connect_provider" "gh" {
  arn = "arn:aws:iam::${data.aws_caller_identity.current.account_id}:oidc-provider/token.actions.githubusercontent.com"
}

resource "aws_iam_role" "gha_deploy" {
  name = "gha-deploy-${var.env}"
  assume_role_policy = jsonencode({
    Statement = [{
      Effect = "Allow"
      Principal = { Federated = data.aws_iam_openid_connect_provider.gh.arn }
      Action = "sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity"
      Condition = {
        StringEquals = { "token.actions.githubusercontent.com:aud" = "sts.amazonaws.com" }
        StringLike   = { "token.actions.githubusercontent.com:sub" = "repo:${var.org}/${var.repo}:environment:${var.env}" }
      }
    }]
  })
}
```

Scope `sub` claim by environment so dev role can't deploy to prod.

### GCP

Workload Identity Federation → Service Account impersonation.

### Azure

OIDC federated identity credentials on Service Principal.

## Branch protection (required)

- `main` requires PR
- All status checks pass
- 1+ reviewer approval (Codeowners for sensitive paths)
- Signed commits (optional but recommended)
- Linear history (squash merge)
- No force push

Configure as code via `github-codeowners` + Terraform `github_branch_protection`
(or repository settings).

## Release workflow

```yaml
# .github/workflows/release.yml
name: release
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
permissions:
  contents: write
  pull-requests: write
jobs:
  release:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: googleapis/release-please-action@v4
        with:
          release-type: simple
          package-name: softco
```

Conventional Commits → automatic CHANGELOG + version bump + tag. Tag triggers
`deploy-prod`.

## PR previews (frontend)

- Vercel: enabled per project, automatic
- Self-hosted: ephemeral Cloud Run / ECS service per PR, torn down on close

---

## Rollback

- App: re-tag previous image SHA in ECS / Cloud Run → automatic rollout
- Infra: `terraform apply` of previous version, or `terraform state rm` +
  re-import
- DB migration: forward-only; if irreversible, restore from PITR snapshot

`make rollback ENV=prod TO=<sha>` documents the standard command.

## Pre-commit hooks (mirror CI locally)

```yaml
# .pre-commit-config.yaml
repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff-pre-commit
    rev: v0.6.9
    hooks:
      - id: ruff
      - id: ruff-format
  - repo: https://github.com/pre-commit/mirrors-mypy
    rev: v1.11.2
    hooks: [{ id: mypy }]
  - repo: https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks
    rev: v8.18.4
    hooks: [{ id: gitleaks }]
  - repo: https://github.com/pre-commit/pre-commit-hooks
    rev: v5.0.0
    hooks:
      - id: check-yaml
      - id: end-of-file-fixer
      - id: trailing-whitespace
      - id: detect-private-key
```

## Never do

- Long-lived cloud access keys in secrets
- Bypassing branch protection
- `latest` Docker tag in prod
- Manual deploy from a developer machine
- Skipping the security scan job
- Deploying without health-check gate
- Storing test secrets in plaintext repo files (use `vars` / `secrets`)
